017package org.apache.juneau.rest.server.filter;
018
019import static org.apache.juneau.commons.utils.Shorts.*;
020
021import java.nio.charset.*;
022import java.security.*;
023import java.util.*;
024
025/**
026 * A server-held CSRF token: a secret minted in this process's memory, embedded into the pages this process
027 * serves, and required back on every state-changing request.
028 *
029 * <h5 class='section'>Why this is a synchronizer token and not a double-submit cookie</h5>
030 * <p>
031 * The cheap, common CSRF design is <i>double submit</i>: the server sets a random value in a cookie, the page
032 * reads it back out and echoes it in a header, and the server accepts the request when the cookie and the header
033 * agree.  It needs no server-side state, which is why it keeps getting reinvented.
034 * <p>
035 * <b>It is unsound for an application on a loopback port, because cookies are scoped by host and ignore the
036 * port.</b>  A cookie set by a page served from <c>http://localhost:3000</c> is sent by the browser to
037 * <c>http://localhost:8790</c> as well &mdash; the port is not part of a cookie's origin.  So any other local
038 * development server, any other tool the developer happens to be running, and any page served by any of them can
039 * plant a cookie that this application would read back and accept as its own.  Under double submit that is a
040 * complete CSRF bypass: the attacker chooses the value, plants it in the cookie, and echoes the same value in the
041 * header.  Both halves match, because the attacker supplied both.
042 * <p>
043 * The token here is instead held only in this object, in this process's memory.  It is written into the served
044 * HTML and compared against the request header.  Nothing the browser stores by host can influence it, so the
045 * port-blindness of cookies is irrelevant.
046 * <p>
047 * Consequently: <b>never place this value in a cookie</b>, and never add a code path that accepts a token read
048 * from one.  Doing so does not weaken the mechanism slightly &mdash; it reintroduces exactly the bypass described
049 * above, because a cookie-borne token is attacker-choosable from any port on the same host.
050 *
051 * <h5 class='section'>Lifetime</h5>
052 * <p>
053 * A token instance is a secret with no expiry and no rotation: it lives as long as the object does.  An
054 * application that constructs one at startup therefore gets per-boot tokens, and a restart invalidates every
055 * token previously embedded in a page.  That is deliberate &mdash; a page held open across a restart is a page
056 * whose server no longer shares any state with it, and requiring a reload is the honest outcome.  Two instances
057 * never share a value, so a token minted by one is rejected by the other.
058 *
059 * <h5 class='section'>Example:</h5>
060 * <p class='bjava'>
061 *    <jc>// One token per process, embedded into every page this process serves.</jc>
062 *    SynchronizerToken <jv>token</jv> = SynchronizerToken.<jsm>generate</jsm>();
063 *    String <jv>html</jv> = <js>"&lt;meta name='csrf-token' content='"</js> + <jv>token</jv>.value() + <js>"'&gt;"</js>;
064 * </p>
065 *
066 * <h5 class='section'>See Also:</h5><ul>
067 *    <li class='jc'>{@link LoopbackBoundary}
068 * </ul>
069 *
070 * @since 10.0.0
071 */
072public final class SynchronizerToken {
073
074   /** Number of random bytes behind a generated token.  256 bits, well beyond guessing range. */
075   private static final int TOKEN_BYTES = 32;
076
077   /** Shared CSPRNG reused across calls to {@link #generate()}; {@link SecureRandom} is thread-safe. */
078   private static final SecureRandom RANDOM = new SecureRandom();
079
080   private final String value;
081
082   /**
083    * Constructor.
084    *
085    * @param value The token value.  Must not be <jk>null</jk> or blank.
086    */
087   private SynchronizerToken(String value) {
088      this.value = value;
089   }
090
091   /**
092    * Mints a new token from {@link SecureRandom}.
093    *
094    * @return A new token holding a fresh 256-bit secret, hex-encoded.
095    */
096   public static SynchronizerToken generate() {
097      var bytes = new byte[TOKEN_BYTES];
098      RANDOM.nextBytes(bytes);
099      return new SynchronizerToken(HexFormat.of().formatHex(bytes));
100   }
101
102   /**
103    * Wraps a caller-supplied token value.
104    *
105    * <p>
106    * Intended for tests and for an application that mints its secret elsewhere.  Prefer {@link #generate()},
107    * which cannot be given a weak value by accident.
108    *
109    * @param value The token value.  Must not be <jk>null</jk> or blank.
110    * @return A token holding {@code value}.
111    * @throws IllegalArgumentException If {@code value} is <jk>null</jk> or blank.
112    */
113   public static SynchronizerToken of(String value) {
114      reqnn("value", value);
115      if (value.isBlank())
116         throw iaex("Argument 'value' must not be blank.");
117      return new SynchronizerToken(value);
118   }
119
120   /**
121    * The token value, for embedding into a served page.
122    *
123    * @return The token value.  Never <jk>null</jk> or blank.
124    */
125   public String value() { return value; }
126
127   /**
128    * Whether {@code candidate} is this token.
129    *
130    * <p>
131    * Compares in time independent of how many leading characters match, so a caller cannot recover the token
132    * one character at a time by measuring how long a rejection takes.  A <jk>null</jk> or blank candidate is
133    * not this token.
134    *
135    * @param candidate The value presented by the request.  Can be <jk>null</jk>.
136    * @return <jk>true</jk> if {@code candidate} equals this token's value.
137    */
138   public boolean matches(String candidate) {
139      if (ie(candidate))
140         return false;
141      return MessageDigest.isEqual(value.getBytes(StandardCharsets.UTF_8), candidate.getBytes(StandardCharsets.UTF_8));
142   }
143
144   /**
145    * Returns a description that does <b>not</b> include the token value.
146    *
147    * <p>
148    * The value is a secret, and a bean-dumping logger or a debug view that stringifies its collaborators would
149    * otherwise write it somewhere it can be read back.
150    *
151    * @return A value-free description.
152    */
153   @Override /* Object */
154   public String toString() { return "SynchronizerToken(value=<redacted>)"; }
155}
